meta.about: The roster of guns the player can carry (docs/unreal/LOADOUT.md 3.2). A gun is one entry here plus one row in attachments.json `compatibility`; nothing in code names a gun. The CHOPPER and the NINE take their rules from config.json and their presentation from presentation.json unchanged (parity, LOADOUT.md 1.2); a new gun carries both blocks inline in exactly those files' schemas, so the same parsers read them.
meta.units: as config.json and presentation.json: metres, seconds, radians (spread, recoil), vertical degrees (adsFov), rounds per minute; presentation in web gun space (x right, y up, z toward the viewer, muzzle at -z). The resolver works in these units on the JSON and only then parses (LOADOUT.md 3.7); ParseGun converts to centimetres and degrees, noise included.
meta.refs: {"$ref": "config.json#weapons.chopper"} is that object (or number) of that file, as it is. Every ref must resolve; MurderInc.Loadout.DataLoads checks that each ref of extraDefaults gives a number.
meta.status: exists = usable now (in the repository, or on the box for pack content); template = an Unreal template asset stands in; procedural = the viewmodel rig plays it from the rules, as the web game does; inProgress = an agent is on it now; inPack = in the purchased pack but not imported or not prepared (no socket, no variant); missing = nobody has started it; notApplicable = the role does not apply to that gun
meta.slot: rules.slot is the roster position; the resolver sets FMIWeaponDef::Slot to the carried slot (1 ... 4)
meta.provisional: markers and reload marks noted as provisional are first values that the pack import replaces; the rule numbers of the new guns are design values (LOADOUT.md 3.2).

ready.about: Which guns the rack offers (LOADOUT.md 3.2). A parity gun is always offered. Any other gun is offered only when it is ready: the mesh of its default variant (stock open) is exists, not a stand-in, and every core role is exists, template or procedural. Inside a ready gun, a slot is offered only when its mount is exists, and a stock option only when its variant is exists. A gun that is not ready is hidden; with the console variable devFlag set to 1 it shows with the DEV tag (frontend.loadout.devTag). A saved set-up that carries a gun that is not ready drops it (LOADOUT.md 7).

ammo.about: The carry cost (LOADOUT.md 3.2.3). Every carried gun with a finite reserve draws on one shared reserve, the bag; a gun with an infinite reserve (the NINE) has none. The bag starts with the largest `reserve` of the carried finite guns (150 for every gun of the roster: the web CHOPPER's), and the Hold the Block resupply goes into the bag once: the flow's AddReserve(90, 240) is unchanged and FMIWeaponRules::AddReserve adds to each pool instead of each gun. With one finite gun (the parity set-up) the bag is that gun's reserve, so every number is the web game's. Extra long guns bring only their loaded magazines.

bag.start: max reserve of the carried finite guns

extraDefaults.about: Fields every gun may set in `extra`. The resolver fills a missing or null field with this default as a number before any effect is applied (LOADOUT.md 3.7), so the CHOPPER and the NINE get exactly the values the web game uses.

falloff.unit: {start m, end m, min share}: full damage to start, linear to min x at end, min beyond; start = end is a step to min

fireModes.unit: every run starts in fireModes[0]; ["semi"] for the NINE

semiFireBuffer.unit: s, the press buffer of an automatic gun switched to semi

modeSwitch.unit: s the selector takes; the gun cannot fire meanwhile

inspectAfter.unit: s idle before the idle inspect plays (presentation only); a gun's own rules.inspectAfter wins

pool.unit: ammo pool id (ammo.pools); ignored for an infinite reserve

extra.notes: Every other extra field takes its default (extraDefaults). The selector lever is modelled on the left side (spec 02 5.2), so semi is offered; every run starts in fireModes[0], auto, as the web game.

optic.notes: The centre of the 106 mm top-cover rail on the lug tops. The front sight's tower, ears and post stand under a scope's line of sight, so the FrontSight bone (a closed shell with its housing capped below it) is hidden for any optic.

muzzle.notes: The booster's base plane on the bore. The Booster bone (a closed shell, X 0.426 to 0.4975) is hidden for any muzzle part; an 8.5 mm barrel stub with its bore stays behind it.

underbarrel.notes: The underside of the folded stock's shoulder plate (a thin curved band that hangs 20 mm under the handguard; the handguard's own bottom is higher, at Z -0.0416). The walnut grip part is a saddle that hugs that plate and carries the weight; the player's palm rests there already (Palm_L).

mounts.notes: at: the socket in the mesh's own frame, metres (x forward along the bore, y left, z up, as the art manifest lists it); MurderInc.Loadout.SocketContract holds it to Content/Data/gun_contract.json. hide: the deform bones that vanish when a part of the slot is fitted. rideBone: the bone a fitted part follows after it is placed, so a magazine part drops and hides with the reload.

shorty.derivation: Our own bullpup carbine (700 mm, the magazine behind the pistol grip) since round 4; until then the pack's Short handguard rifle. The numbers did not change with the art. From the STICK by the factors of LOADOUT.md 3.2.1: a short gas system (rpm 800 -> 860), quick hands (adsTime x 0.9, holster and draw x 0.92), better on the move (moveHip x 0.9), shorter near walls (wallPull x 0.86); it pays with kick (pitch, shake, rise, back x 1.1), a wider aimed cone (ads x 1.15), flash x 1.3, noise 45 -> 50 m and a falloff from 20 to 45 m down to 0.8 x.

reload.notes: provisional: the CHOPPER's marks x 0.95 to the tug. No press check on a tactical reload; on an empty reload the bolt is locked back and the bolt catch closes it at slideRelease (the parser's name for 'the locked bolt or slide closes'). Retimed to the pack's reload notifies by ANIMATION.md.

meshOffset.note: the mesh's frame in gun space (web). SK_Shorty has its origin on the bore at the butt face and its muzzle on +X, so the rotation is the identity, as for SK_Nine (the pack rifles needed a quarter turn because they face +Y). pos moves the butt back so that its Palm_R lands where the CHOPPER's Palm_R is in gun space (web 0.0155, -0.085, -0.040): every view, pose and melee key in config.json is authored for that gun space, so the hip, the sprint, the reload and the strikes all keep the firing hand where it was. (The specification asked for views[0] to be moved instead; that moves one pose only. Worked out by tools/data/make_gun_contract.py.)

clipRoles.about: The first-person states every gun needs a clip for, by role. The asset of a role is A_FP_<Set>_<Role> (spec 02 5.x naming; ANIMATION.md maps each pack clip onto it). Timed roles are stretched to the rules' length (play rate = clip length / rule length) with their notifies on the rules' marks: the rules are the clock, never the clip (ARCHITECTURE 1.3). A role a set lacks falls back as listed; a missing fallback plays nothing and changes no rule. A gun's `clips.byStatus` lists every role once (DataLoads checks it).
